notes: The source is the University of Oregon GC3 core, not UC Davis. The docx URL (labelled 'updated 9-2024' in search results) 301-redirects to research.uoregon.edu, so the file is not retrievable and there is no rate history or effective date. I fetched the live rates page, https://gc3f.uoregon.edu/rates. It lists NovaSeq 6000 (S4, S1, SP), NextSeq 2000, MiSeq i100/Classic and PacBio Revio, with internal and external rates. It lists no NovaSeq X and no AVITI, and it shows no effective date. A search snippet says an older UO NovaSeq page showed rates effective 1 Jul 2022. I could not run the local zipfile extraction because no shell tool was available in this session. The UC CAT comparison (25B 150PE lane $2,600) is therefore not possible for this source. Only one weak item came out of it: an Oregon core still sells only the 6000 and NextSeq 2000 at undated rates.
how_to_mine: Not worth a deep extraction. Optional follow-up: check web.archive.org snapshots of gc3f.uoregon.edu/rates to see when, or whether, NovaSeq X rates appear, and compare the 6000 S4 price over time. For UC Davis, search 'dnatech.genomecenter.ucdavis.edu' rates pages directly (NovaSeq X 25B and AVITI) rather than this docx.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: A University of Oregon core still lists only NovaSeq 6000 flow cells (no NovaSeq X) on its live rate page.
items.detail: gc3f.uoregon.edu/rates (fetched Oct 2026, undated) lists NovaSeq 6000 S4 300-cycle at $5,070 internal / $6,903 external, S1 300-cycle at $3,897 / $5,305, and SP 300-cycle at $2,318 / $3,158. It shows no NovaSeq X or AVITI line. This is small-core evidence that some academic sites remain on the 6000. The rate-card page has no effective date, so it could be stale.
items.source_name: University of Oregon Genomics & Cell Characterization Core Facility
items.why_new: The Oregon core is not among the core rate cards already used, and it shows a 6000-only research core.
